hypotheses.hypothesis: The postpartum HLA-II^hi / CD64^hi APC subset split reflects a transient monocyte-to-DC reprogramming window where loss of progesterone-driven GR/PR signaling unmasks a CD64+ inflammatory APC state that seeds MS relapse, distinct from steady-state APC remodeling captured by V22/V32.
hypotheses.why_new_or_underexplored: Postpartum relapse biology is clinically known but the CD64/HLA-II axis split has not been mechanistically linked to hormone-withdrawal-driven APC lineage drift in this project beyond being flagged dormant.
hypotheses.testable_prediction: Within 4–12 weeks postpartum, MS relapsers will show a CD64^hi HLA-DR^hi CD14^int monocyte-derived APC population with elevated FCGR1A, IFI30, and CTSS versus non-relapsers, and this population will not be captured by V22/V32 signatures alone.
data_to_test_now: public postpartum PBMC scRNA-seq (e.g., Edahiro/MS pregnancy cohorts)
bulk MS pregnancy transcriptomic time series
FCGR1A/HLA-DRA co-expression in existing APC atlases stratified by sex/parity
hypotheses.risk_of_artifact: Parity metadata is sparse and confounded by treatment washout; CD64 upregulation can also reflect generic IFN-γ exposure unrelated to relapse.
hypotheses.therapeutic_or_biomarker_angle: CD64+HLA-DR+ APC frequency as a postpartum relapse-risk biomarker; transient FcγRI or CSF1R modulation in the postpartum window.
hypotheses.minimum_grounding_test: Confirm in ≥1 public postpartum PBMC dataset that CD64/HLA-DR co-high APCs are quantifiable and differ from V22/V32 loadings.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MS APC dysfunction is partially driven by a shifted lysosomal pH/protease setpoint (CTSS, CTSB, LGMN, IFI30, CLN-family) that biases self-peptide editing on HLA-II independent of HLA allele, coupling to the V26 MIF/CD74/IFN-APC structure.
hypotheses.why_new_or_underexplored: V26 implicates lysosomal processing but the project has not directly tested a pH/protease stoichiometry hypothesis as a quantitative APC phenotype separable from HLA-II abundance.
hypotheses.testable_prediction: A CTSS/CTSB/LGMN/IFI30 ratio score will separate MS from control APCs more sharply than HLA-DR expression alone and will correlate with CD74 surface retention.
hypotheses.risk_of_artifact: Cathepsin transcripts are highly activation-state dependent; bulk dissociation can inflate lysosomal gene signal in monocytes.
hypotheses.therapeutic_or_biomarker_angle: Selective cathepsin S inhibitors or v-ATPase modulators as APC-editing therapy; lysosomal-ratio score as APC-state biomarker.
hypotheses.minimum_grounding_test: Compute the protease ratio score in one MS scRNA-seq dataset and check it is non-redundant with HLA-DRA loading.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Choroid plexus epithelial and stromal cells, not adaptive immune cells, set the CSF complement (C1q/C3/CFB) and IFN tone that licenses border-associated macrophage APC remodeling in MS, making the CP a non-adaptive driver of the V26 axis.
hypotheses.why_new_or_underexplored: Pushes outside canonical T/B adaptive immunity into CNS-barrier stromal biology rarely integrated with the project's APC framework.
hypotheses.testable_prediction: CP epithelial cells in MS will show coordinated upregulation of C3, CFB, ISG15, IFI27 and ICAM1, and CP-adjacent macrophages will show the V26 HLA-II/CD74/IFI30 program more strongly than parenchymal microglia.
data_to_test_now: published CP scRNA-seq (Reboldi, Yang et al.)
hypotheses.risk_of_artifact: CP is fragile in postmortem tissue; complement transcripts can be induced by dissociation/ischemia.
hypotheses.therapeutic_or_biomarker_angle: CSF complement-split products as compartment-specific MS activity biomarker; localized complement modulation at the CP barrier.
hypotheses.minimum_grounding_test: Show CP epithelial complement+IFN co-module exists and is MS-enriched in one public dataset.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Circadian control via BMAL1/REV-ERBα in myeloid cells gates the HLA-II/CD74/IFI30 APC program, and loss of circadian amplitude (shift work, sleep disruption) phenocopies the V26 remodeling state — a non-adaptive systems driver of MS APC dysregulation.
hypotheses.why_new_or_underexplored: Circadian myeloid biology is largely absent from the project's APC framing despite epidemiologic shift-work/MS links.
hypotheses.testable_prediction: Time-of-sampling and BMAL1/NR1D1 expression will explain a measurable fraction of variance in HLA-DR/CD74/IFI30 module scores in MS PBMC datasets, and REV-ERB agonism will dampen the module in monocytes in vitro.
